Read the cue points and labels of a wave file

Source: R/wavCues.R
wavCues.Rd

A wave file marks positions in a recording with cue points, and names them in a separate list, which is how an editor saves the markers and labelled regions someone has put on a recording. This reads both and gives them back together, one row per cue point, in the order the file holds them.

Usage

wavCues(x, output = "Annotation")

Arguments

x

Path to a wave file, or a raw vector holding one

output

One of "Annotation" or "data.frame".

Value

A list of Annotation objects, one per cue point, or with output "data.frame" a data frame of one row per cue point, with its identifier, position, position in seconds, label, note, region length, purpose, region text and the chunk its position is into. A file holding no cue points and no labels gives an empty list, or a data frame of no rows.

Details

The position of a cue point is a sample offset into the audio, counted in frames rather than bytes, and seconds converts it by the sample rate the file declares. chunk is the chunk the offset is into, which is data for an ordinary recording; a file that keeps its audio in a wave list can point a cue at one part of it, and then the offset is into that part rather than into the recording.

A labelled region carries a length in samples and a purpose, commonly rgn, where a plain marker carries neither. label is the short name of a point, note a longer comment on it, and text the text of a labelled region, each as the file's own list gives it.

A label whose cue point is missing is still reported, with no position: the text is metadata the file carries, and dropping it because the chunk that places it has been lost would be reporting less than the file holds. A cue point with no label is likewise reported with no text; nine files in a cached copy of bio.acousti.ca declare 99 such points, all of them at position zero, which is a writer reserving the room rather than marking anything.

By default each cue point is given as an Annotation object. A labelled region is an annotation of type region running from its position for its length, and any other point an annotation of type cue that starts and ends at its position. The value of the annotation is the label of the point, or failing that the text of its region; its source is wavCues, its file the path read, and its metadata the fields of its row in the data frame other than seconds. An annotation whose position is not known, or not known in seconds, starts and ends at NA.

See also

wavChunks() lists the chunks a file holds, and wavInfo() reads the text of the same labels without the positions they belong to. writeAudacityLabels() writes the annotations as an Audacity label file.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cues <- wavCues("marked.wav", output="data.frame")
cues[!is.na(cues$label), c("seconds", "label")]
writeAudacityLabels(wavCues("marked.wav"), "marked.txt")
} # }
